candidates.source_name: European Commission – DG ENLARGEMENT: Montenegro country page (enlargement package hub)
candidates.why_relevant: Central hub linking every annual Montenegro country report, enlargement package SWDs, Reform Agenda/Growth Plan documents and press material. From here all Chapter 9 (financial services) and Chapter 4 (free movement of capital / payments) assessments are reachable each autumn.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual scheduled crawl (Oct-Nov enlargement package) + quarterly re-crawl of document listing; harvest PDFs and diff Chapter 9 / Chapter 4 sections year-on-year.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro report 2025 chapter 9 financial services

candidates.source_name: European Commission – Montenegro 2025 Report SWD(2025) 754 final (annual progress report PDF)
candidates.why_relevant: The single most benchmark-dense annual document on Montenegrin banking/payments alignment: Chapter 9 financial services, Chapter 4 capital movement/payment services, AML, deposit guarantee scheme, SEPA/TIPS-Clone commitments, plus forward-looking recommendations for the next 12 months.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Direct PDF fetch once per year; text-extract and section-split by chapter heading; retain prior years for delta analysis.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro report 2025 chapter 9 financial services

candidates.source_name: EU u Crnoj Gori / EUME – 'Poglavlje 9 – Finansijske usluge' (EU Delegation & Montenegro EU-info portal)
candidates.why_relevant: Local-language explainer and document hub for negotiating Chapter 9 (finansijske usluge): closing benchmarks, negotiating position, state of play, and links to national implementing bodies. Also explains how the EC report is produced ('Kako nastaje Izvještaj Evropske komisije o Crnoj Gori?'), which reveals the national input chain worth tracking.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of chapter pages and news feed in sr; snowball outbound links to ministries and CBCG.
queries_used: "Izvještaj Evropske komisije" Crna Gora 2025 poglavlje 9 finansijske usluge pregovori

candidates.source_name: European Parliament – rapporteur report on the Commission reports on Montenegro (A10-0093/2025)
candidates.why_relevant: Parliamentary scrutiny layer over the Commission's assessment; frequently sharpens or politicises findings on AML, banking supervision independence and financial-sector governance, and signals which reform commitments face EU-side pressure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual keyword search of the EP document register (doceo) for 'Montenegro'; fetch HTML and extract financial-sector paragraphs.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro report 2025 chapter 9 financial services
Montenegro Economic Reform Programme ERP European Commission joint conclusions financial sector 2025

candidates.source_name: European Commission DG ECFIN – Economic Reform Programmes: Commission overview and country assessments (incl. Montenegro)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual macro-financial assessment of Montenegro's ERP includes a dedicated financial-sector section (credit growth, NPLs, supervisory and risk-management reporting frameworks) and explicit policy guidance the authorities must act on — a reliable early indicator of coming banking-regulation changes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch (spring publication cycle) of the institutional-paper PDF; extract the Montenegro country chapter.
queries_used: Montenegro Economic Reform Programme ERP European Commission joint conclusions financial sector 2025

candidates.source_name: Council of the EU – Joint Conclusions of the Economic and Financial Dialogue between the EU and the Western Balkans and Türkiye
candidates.why_relevant: The ECOFIN-level country-specific policy guidance to Montenegro; the financial-sector recommendations here (e.g. strengthening banking reporting and risk-management frameworks) are agreed commitments that national regulators then translate into law and bylaws.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual (May) query of the Council public document register for 'ECOFIN Western Balkans joint conclusions'; store the PDF and extract the Montenegro section.
queries_used: Montenegro Economic Reform Programme ERP European Commission joint conclusions financial sector 2025

candidates.source_name: EEAS – EU Delegation to Montenegro (press releases and dialogue documents)
candidates.why_relevant: Publishes the local mirror of EU-Montenegro economic dialogue outputs and press statements, often in both English and Montenegrin, and earlier than the central Brussels portals index them.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the delegation news listing; filter for economy/finance keywords in en and sr.
queries_used: Montenegro Economic Reform Programme ERP European Commission joint conclusions financial sector 2025

candidates.source_name: IMF – Montenegro Article IV Consultation staff reports (Country Report series)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual, deeply quantitative assessment of Montenegro's banking system: capital, liquidity, asset quality, cash-loan and real-estate credit dynamics, macroprudential measures, plus a statistical annex with financial soundness indicators. Also flags payment-system integration (SEPA, TIPS Clone).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch of the CR PDF (source-pdf mirror is directly downloadable); table-extract FSI annex into a time series.
queries_used: IMF Article IV Montenegro 2025 banking sector

candidates.source_name: IMF – Montenegro mission concluding statements and Executive Board press releases
candidates.why_relevant: Concluding statements appear weeks-to-months before the full staff report and already contain the substantive banking-supervision and AML messages; the Board press release adds the official assessment. Best early-warning channel in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the IMF Montenegro country news feed monthly; capture HTML of concluding statements and PR items.
queries_used: IMF Article IV Montenegro 2025 banking sector

candidates.source_name: IMF – FSAP country index for Montenegro
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative index of Montenegro's Financial Sector Assessment Program participation and the resulting FSSA/technical notes. FSAPs are the deepest available third-party diagnostic of supervision, crisis management, deposit insurance and payment infrastructure — low frequency but very high value.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Semi-annual check for a new FSAP cycle; alert if a mission or update is announced (last joint IMF/WB FSAP mission reported for Sept 2015).
queries_used: IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program FSAP Montenegro 2015 technical assistance report

candidates.source_name: World Bank – Montenegro FSAP Technical Note on Financial Infrastructure (payments and settlement systems)
candidates.why_relevant: Rare, granular independent assessment of Montenegro's national payment system (RTGS/DNS), oversight arrangements, credit registry and collateral registry — the structural baseline against which later SEPA/TIPS/instant-payments moves should be read.
candidates.legal_status: CC-BY-compatible World Bank open access terms
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off archival fetch; re-check the World Bank Documents & Reports API for any FSAP update for Montenegro.
queries_used: IMF Financial Sector Assessment Program FSAP Montenegro 2015 technical assistance report

candidates.source_name: World Bank – Montenegro country page and Country Partnership Framework FY25-29
candidates.why_relevant: Hub for the CPF, project pipeline and press releases; the CPF and DPO operations name financial-sector resilience and EU-market integration objectives, exposing planned reform conditionality before it reaches national law.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of the country overview + news; query the Documents & Reports API (country=Montenegro, majdocty=Country Focus) for new strategy/diagnostic documents.
queries_used: World Bank Montenegro financial sector Systematic Country Diagnostic Country Partnership Framework

candidates.source_name: World Bank – Montenegro Systematic Country Diagnostic (and SCD Update)
candidates.why_relevant: Identifies structural constraints including banking-sector vulnerabilities, limits of the central bank's lender-of-last-resort function under euroisation, and credit-market frictions — framing that shapes subsequent lending operations and reform dialogue.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Archival fetch; monitor Open Knowledge Repository entity page for new editions.
queries_used: World Bank Montenegro financial sector Systematic Country Diagnostic Country Partnership Framework

candidates.source_name: World Bank Open Knowledge Repository / Documents & Reports (Montenegro filter)
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-queryable archive of every World Bank Montenegro document (FSAP notes, Western Balkans Regular Economic Reports, project appraisal documents) with stable bitstream URLs and an open API — the most automatable entry point in this cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled API query (DSpace REST / Documents & Reports search API) filtered on country=Montenegro and finance/payments topics; incremental by publication date.
queries_used: World Bank Montenegro financial sector Systematic Country Diagnostic Country Partnership Framework

candidates.source_name: EBRD – Montenegro Country Strategy (2021-2026 and draft 2026-2031)
candidates.why_relevant: Country strategies contain an explicit financial-sector diagnostic (bank concentration, SME finance gap, capital-market depth, digitalisation) and set out the EBRD's planned interventions — a forward view of where donor money and technical assistance will hit Montenegrin banks.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch strategy PDF at each 5-year cycle plus the public consultation drafts; also monitor EBRD project summary documents for Montenegrin bank credit lines.
queries_used: EBRD Montenegro banking transition report country strategy Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: EBRD Transition Report – Montenegro country assessment (annual)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual two-to-four page country assessment with transition-quality scores including a 'competitive/resilient' financial-sector dimension, plus a short list of the year's key financial-sector policy developments. Comparable across Western Balkan peers.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual (autumn) fetch of the Montenegro country-assessment PDF from the Transition Report microsite; store scores as a time series.
queries_used: EBRD Montenegro banking transition report country strategy Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: EIB – CESEE Bank Lending Survey (Vienna Initiative), Montenegro country slice
candidates.why_relevant: Semi-annual survey of parent banking groups and local subsidiaries covering credit supply/demand, cross-border funding intentions and NPL expectations, with per-country breakdowns for Montenegro. Structured, downloadable data and forward-looking bank strategy signals unavailable from national sources.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Twice-yearly fetch of the survey report plus any accompanying data annex; extract the Montenegro panel.
queries_used: Vienna Initiative CESEE Bank Lending Survey EIB Montenegro Western Balkans

candidates.source_name: Vienna Initiative (European Bank Coordination Initiative) – reports and working groups
candidates.why_relevant: Cross-institutional forum (EC, EIB, EBRD, IMF, World Bank, home/host supervisors) producing working-group reports on NPLs, cross-border supervision, capital-market development and digitalisation in CESEE, routinely covering Montenegro as a host country.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly crawl of the publications/type listings; filter titles and bodies for Montenegro/Western Balkans.
queries_used: Vienna Initiative CESEE Bank Lending Survey EIB Montenegro Western Balkans

candidates.source_name: Council of Europe MONEYVAL – evaluations hub and Montenegro mutual evaluation / follow-up reports
candidates.why_relevant: Fifth-round mutual evaluation of Montenegro (published Feb 2024, adopted Dec 2023) plus annual follow-up reports re-rating FATF recommendations. Directly assesses regulation and supervision of financial institutions, CDD, new technologies and virtual assets — the strongest external constraint on Montenegrin banks' and PSPs' compliance obligations.
candidates.legal_status: Council of Europe reproduction terms; attribution required
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor plenary outcome pages (typically 2-3 plenaries/year) and the country page; fetch MER/FUR PDFs from rm.coe.int and extract recommendation-rating tables.
queries_used: MONEYVAL Montenegro mutual evaluation report follow-up AML Council of Europe

candidates.source_name: FATF – Global Network page for MONEYVAL (and FATF statements affecting Montenegro)
candidates.why_relevant: Confirms the methodology and rating framework behind MONEYVAL findings and is the venue where grey-listing risk for Montenegro would materialise — a step change for correspondent banking and payments if it ever occurred.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor FATF plenary outcome statements three times a year for Montenegro mentions.
queries_used: MONEYVAL Montenegro mutual evaluation report follow-up AML Council of Europe

candidates.source_name: ecoi.net – archived copies of EU and Council of Europe country documents on Montenegro
candidates.why_relevant: Independent mirror/archive of enlargement-package SWDs and related assessments with stable document IDs; useful fallback when Commission download links rotate, and a convenient way to enumerate document history.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use only as a fallback resolver for missing/moved primary PDFs; do not treat as authoritative text.
queries_used: European Commission Montenegro report 2025 chapter 9 financial services

negative_findings.description: None of the core supranational assessors in this cell (IMF, World Bank, EBRD, EIB, MONEYVAL) appear to publish their Montenegro financial-sector assessments in Montenegrin/Serbian. Searches using sr terms returned only national-media relays and the EU-funded eu.me portal, never an official sr-language version of an Article IV report, Transition Report assessment or MONEYVAL MER.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language coverage of this cell is effectively second-hand: sr-language material exists only as journalism, government press releases, or EU-info-portal explainers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any sr-language monitoring for this cell must target relays and national counterparts, not the assessors themselves; and translation drift in media relays is a real accuracy risk.

negative_findings.description: The only Montenegro FSAP material located dates to the joint IMF/World Bank FSAP mission of September 2015 (technical notes published around January 2016). No evidence of a newer FSAP or FSAP Update for Montenegro was found in the searches performed.
negative_findings.result_summary: FSAP-grade payments/supervision diagnostics for Montenegro are roughly a decade old.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deepest structural view of Montenegro's payment infrastructure predates SEPA accession and TIPS-Clone plans, so Article IV annexes and EC Chapter 9 sections must carry that analytical load instead.

negative_findings.description: A dedicated MONEYVAL Montenegro country landing page URL was not isolated in these searches; individual reports were reached via the general evaluations page, plenary-outcome news items, and direct rm.coe.int document links whose slugs are opaque.
negative_findings.result_summary: Report discovery for MONEYVAL depends on plenary news pages rather than a predictable per-country document index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection needs a crawler over plenary outcome pages plus rm.coe.int link extraction, not a simple country-page poll.

negative_findings.description: Searches repeatedly surfaced the Central Bank of Montenegro annual report (cbcg.me) and gov.me ERP pages as the national counterparties of these supranational assessments; they are national actors and therefore belong to other coverage cells, not this one.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not recorded as candidates here to avoid duplicating another cell's scope.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Cross-cell linkage matters: supranational recommendations should be joined to CBCG/gov.me implementation documents during analysis.

coverage_gaps.description: Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF), EU4Business/EFSE and the Regional Cooperation Council were not searched in this pass, although they fund and assess Montenegrin financial intermediaries and SME lending.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass over wbif.eu, coebank.org, efse.lu and rcc.int filtered on Montenegro financial-sector operations and assessments.

coverage_gaps.description: No payments-specific supranational assessor was located for Montenegro beyond the 2015 World Bank FSAP technical note — e.g. CPMI/BIS red-book style coverage, or SEPA/EPC-side accession documentation assessing Montenegrin scheme compliance.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe the European Payments Council SEPA participation documentation and BIS/CPMI country coverage for Montenegro; also check ECB convergence/Western Balkans workshop outputs.

coverage_gaps.description: Candidates in this cell are overwhelmingly PDF/HTML narrative. Machine-readable series (IMF FSI database, World Bank Global Financial Development / Findex, EBRD Banking Environment and Performance) were not explicitly enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a follow-up pass to register the IMF FSI, IMF data API, World Bank indicator API and Global Findex Montenegro slices as structured-data sources with API-based collection.

coverage_gaps.description: No sr-language primary document from any supranational assessor was found; local-language coverage of this cell rests on media and EU-info relays only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Track sr-language government translations of EC recommendations (Ministry of European Affairs / Programme of Accession) as the local-language proxy layer for this cell, coordinating with the national-actor cell to avoid duplication.

coverage_gaps.description: Several large PDFs (EC enlargement document-download endpoints, EBRD dam/ asset paths, IMF media source-pdf paths) use rotating or CDN-style URLs that may change between publication cycles; none were fetch-tested in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Have the deterministic verification pass resolve each PDF link and, where fragile, store a landing-page URL plus a title-based re-discovery query rather than the raw asset path.

brief: Montenegro's banking and payments sector is unusually well covered by supranational assessors: the European Commission's annual enlargement report (Chapter 9 financial services, Chapter 4 capital/payments) and the ERP/ECOFIN economic-dialogue cycle set reform benchmarks, the IMF's annual Article IV provides the quantitative banking diagnostic plus forward-looking supervisory and AML messages, and MONEYVAL's fifth-round evaluation and annual follow-ups drive the AML compliance agenda for banks and PSPs. The World Bank, EBRD and EIB add strategy-level and survey-level views — notably the 2015 joint FSAP technical note on payment and settlement infrastructure, EBRD country strategies and Transition Report assessments, and the semi-annual Vienna-Initiative CESEE Bank Lending Survey with a Montenegro slice. All of this is published in English on stable institutional domains with permissive reuse terms, making the cell highly automatable via annual/semi-annual scheduled fetches and the World Bank document APIs; the main weaknesses are the decade-old FSAP baseline, the absence of any payments-specific supranational assessment covering the SEPA/TIPS-Clone era, and the complete lack of sr-language primary documents, which forces local-language monitoring onto national media relays and the eu.me portal.
